summary: Maries County towersite bought in the 1940s; a wood tower was planned in 1948 and a new fire tower erected in 1967-68. No source describes the site today.

events.note: Land acquired for a towersite in fiscal 1945-46 (240 acres per the annual report); the Spring Creek Gap page dates a 280-acre purchase to 1948
Bland Courier item quoted on the lookout page: a wood tower would soon be under construction north of Vichy near Highway 63. Completion is not confirmed.
Used as a Ground Observer Corps observation post in the 1950s (decade only)
Wooden fire tower cab completely remodeled, fiscal 1958-59
New fire tower erected, fiscal 1967-68; the source does not say what it replaced

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on acreage (240 acres in the 1945-46 report and the 1947-48 manual; 280 acres in the MDC Spring Creek Gap page) and on the acquisition date (1945-46 vs 1948). The 1948 newspaper item is quoted second-hand on the lookout page, so the date the wood tower was finished is unknown. The 1967-68 new tower is the last tower reference found; its design and whether it replaced the wood tower are unknown. The 2018 Central Region towersites plan (https://mdc.mo.gov/sites/default/files/2020-12/2018%20Central%20Region%20Towers%20Area%20Plan.pdf) lists other Maries County sites (Freeburg) but I found no mention of Vichy in it; worth checking. No source describes the tower or its footings now; the brief's status stays unknown and no access facts are set, because the Spring Creek Gap page does not mention the tower. Ownership: the 1947-48 manual says the Missouri Conservation Commission owned the towersite.
